html:
The Chelamela were a band of the Kalapuya people of Oregon's Willamette Valley, living along the Long Tom River west of today's Eugene.

Like other Kalapuya, they gathered camas roots and acorns and set fires to keep the valley open for game and plants. Disease in the 1830s killed most of them. After settlers on the Oregon Trail filled the valley, the survivors signed the treaty of 1855 and were moved to the Grand Ronde reservation, alongside the Molalla.
sum: The Chelamela were a band of the Kalapuya people of Oregon's Willamette Valley, living along the Long Tom River west of today's Eugene.
